function: Excluded as system: learned CIR spatial super-resolution (BiLSTM plus BasicVSR) on single-antenna links, one transmitting antenna and omnidirectional receiving points, no RIS (p. 9, p. 4).
notes: Checks 1 to 5 pass: research article (TWC 2024, title on p. 1 matches the DOI), proposes and evaluates a learned method (p. 9), and the learned function is spatial prediction or synthesis of the channel, an area 2 type problem: "the problem of CIR super-resolution is estimating the unknown {yi,j,t } given {xi,j,t } are known" (p. 5). Check 6 (system) applies: "In each scenario, one transmitting antenna is deployed, and 256 × 256 receiving points" (p. 9); "each antenna elements has been considered as an ideal omni-directional antenna" (p. 4); the CIR h(t) is the response between one transmitting antenna and one receiving antenna (p. 1, p. 4). The receiving points are positions over an area of about 89 m by 139 m (p. 9), not a MIMO array, and no MIMO channel matrix is modelled. No RIS or reflecting surface appears anywhere in the paper. MIMO and "multi-antenna wireless channel characterizations" appear only as motivation (p. 1). If the reviewer rejects the area 2 reading of the function (radio-map or channel-modelling task rather than channel estimation), the first code that applies would be function instead of system. For reference: ray-tracing dataset of London outdoor scenes at 28 GHz, 467 training and 454 test scenarios (p. 8), compared with bilinear and bicubic interpolation and image and video super-resolution models (p. 10), MSE_dB 31.14 dB on test (p. 10).
